A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 21-page versions of the same Proximal-IMH paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on bimodal targets, MNIST inverse imaging and nonlinear Helmholtz scattering in Sections 4.1-4.3, with additional empirical diagnostics in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original numerical experiments and appendix diagnostics, including sampling convergence, reconstruction results and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The approximate-posterior proposal, proximal correction, linear transformation and nonlinear single-step Gauss-Newton procedure are unchanged. The acceptance formulas and practical omission of nonlinear Jacobian determinant ratios are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same Gaussian proposal comparisons, synthetic bimodal targets, MNIST imaging and nonlinear Helmholtz scattering, including the same operator-perturbation and grid scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains Approx-IMH, Latent-IMH, NUTS, MALA and the Approx-NUTS histogram comparison. Figures 6 and 8 retain Approx-IMH and NUTS, and Appendix C retains the DCT versus ILU preconditioning comparison.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, noise levels, dimensions, operator constructions and testing procedures are unchanged in Sections 3-4 and Appendix C. For example, both retain the 15%-20% observational noise-to-signal range and the same fine/coarse Helmholtz grids.

E4.justification: The KL sensitivity studies, beta sweeps, operator-discrepancy analysis, Jacobian determinant diagnostics and supplementary Helmholtz analyses are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: The five-trial reporting in Figures 2 and 6 is unchanged. Figure 11 retains the same 2,000-sample and random-pair diagnostics and 5%-95% quantile reporting; no new uncertainty procedure or seed information appears.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted curves, reconstruction examples and reported findings are unchanged. The main-text result figures and all appendix results retain the same content, with no added or corrected outcomes.

T1.justification: The assumptions, KL-divergence formulas, mixing-time statements and nonlinear derivations are unchanged. Appendix A's proofs and Appendix B's forward-model and adjoint derivations are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about proximal proposals, theoretical advantages under stated assumptions and empirical sampling improvements.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the restricted theoretical assumptions, neglected nonlinear Jacobian terms and dependence on approximation quality and beta.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgements on page 9 identify computing time on TACC's Stampede system. This adds limited computing-resource provenance without establishing changed experimental settings; the existing technical details in Appendix C remain identical.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Latent-IMH, multifidelity sampling and other approaches are unchanged. The bibliography is reflowed across pages 9-10 without adding or removing research references.

P1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgements section, slightly expands the institutional affiliation and replaces the preprint notice with ICML proceedings information. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded publication footnote and new acknowledgements cause limited text, equation and bibliography reflow. All 13 figures and four tables retain their content and presentation, and the appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 adds publication, funding and limited computing-resource information, while preserving the scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations and appendices. These attribution and provenance additions do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
